title: C#: from the first program to reliable .NET applications
summary: 48 detailed lessons from first programs through language mechanisms, reliable systems and independently designed projects.

lessons.title: Source, compilation and the first observable result
lessons.outcome: Build and run Program.cs and check a computed result instead of trusting printed text.
lessons.lab: Write a program calculating the number of seats in four rows of six seats. Check 24 explicitly.
lessons.verification: The program computes 24 seats and the check passes silently.

lessons.title: Types, variables and explicit conversions
lessons.outcome: Choose numeric types deliberately, convert explicitly and parse text with TryParse instead of exceptions.
lessons.lab: Write a TryParse-based validator accepting only nonnegative whole-number quantities.
lessons.verification: 42 is accepted; -1, 4.5 and empty text are rejected without an exception.

lessons.title: Numeric range, checked overflow and decimal amounts
lessons.outcome: Detect integer overflow with checked arithmetic and calculate money with decimal and a named rounding rule.
lessons.lab: Calculate a decimal subtotal and tax, rounding only the final payable amount.
lessons.verification: Subtotal 25.35, unrounded tax 2.091375 and payable 27.44.

lessons.title: Strings, interpolation and Unicode text
lessons.outcome: Compare, transform and measure strings with explicit culture and Unicode policies.
lessons.lab: Implement case-insensitive machine-key comparison with an explicit policy.
lessons.verification: Keys that differ only by ASCII case match; a different separator does not.

lessons.title: Boolean decisions and exhaustive alternatives
lessons.outcome: Write complete, non-overlapping decisions with if statements and switch expressions, including boundary values.
lessons.lab: Write a classifier for negative, zero and positive temperatures.
lessons.verification: -5, 0 and 12 are classified as below zero, zero and above zero.

lessons.title: Loops, invariants and termination
lessons.outcome: Write loops with a stated invariant and termination condition, including empty and not-found cases.
lessons.lab: Implement a first-match search returning a separate not-found representation.
lessons.verification: The first 7 is at index 1; a missing target and an empty array both return false.

lessons.title: Methods, parameters and return contracts
lessons.outcome: Write methods with validated parameters and explicit return contracts that reject invalid input.
lessons.lab: Write a method computing an area from validated nonnegative dimensions.
lessons.verification: 3 by 4 gives 12, a zero side gives 0, and a negative side throws.

lessons.title: Arrays, indices and rectangular data
lessons.outcome: Tell array aliases from copies and traverse rectangular arrays with bounds taken from the data.
lessons.lab: Compute each row sum of the two-by-three grid.
lessons.verification: The row sums are 6 and 15.

lessons.title: Lists, capacity and safe mutation
lessons.outcome: Filter and mutate lists safely, telling capacity from count and copies from in-place changes.
lessons.lab: Produce a filtered list while preserving the original.
lessons.verification: The new list holds 2 and 4 while the original still has four items.

lessons.title: Dictionaries, sets and identity policies
lessons.outcome: Count and deduplicate with dictionaries and sets under an explicit comparer, keeping a present zero distinct from absence.
lessons.lab: Build a frequency dictionary from a list of tags.
lessons.verification: red counts 2 and blue counts 1.

lessons.title: Nullability and optional information
lessons.outcome: Represent missing information with nullable types and keep missing, zero and present values distinct.
lessons.lab: Write a formatter preserving missing, zero and positive measurements.
lessons.verification: null, 0 and 5 are formatted as missing, zero and 5 units.

lessons.title: Value copies, references and mutation ownership
lessons.outcome: Predict copying and sharing for structs and classes and choose the right kind for a value or shared state.
lessons.lab: Choose a representation for a coordinate and for a shared session, explaining the difference.
lessons.verification: Changing the copied coordinate leaves the original at 1, while both session variables see 3.

lessons.title: Classes, constructors and encapsulated invariants
lessons.outcome: Encapsulate state in a class whose constructor and methods keep its invariants on every path.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Preserve a nonnegative balance) and Example B (Reject malformed operations) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: Spending 4 succeeds; spending 7 afterward fails without changing 6. Negative spending is rejected and zero is an accepted no-op.

lessons.title: Records, structs and data equality
lessons.outcome: Use records and structs for value equality and explain what a shallow with-copy shares.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Equal data with distinct identities) and Example B (Notice nested shared state) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: Equal records can be distinct objects; with preserves the previous age. Both records see the appended list item.

lessons.title: Patterns and explicit state models
lessons.outcome: Model explicit states with records and pattern matching so each state carries only its own data.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Narrow before using a value) and Example B (Represent results without impossible combinations) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The same method distinguishes type, value range and string shape. Success carries a count; failure carries a reason.

lessons.title: Foundation project: a validated inventory report
lessons.outcome: Build a validated inventory importer that reports accepted totals and rejected lines deterministically.
lessons.lab: Build a sorted text report from the accepted dictionary and the rejection count.
lessons.verification: The report lists apple: 3, pear: 3 and rejected: 1 in that order.

lessons.title: Interfaces and substitutable behavior
lessons.outcome: Program against an interface so different policies can be substituted without changing the consumer.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Use a declared contract) and Example B (Change policy without changing the consumer) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: Four units cost 12 and zero units cost zero. The same consumer applies a capped or uncapped policy.

lessons.title: Generics and constraints that express capabilities
lessons.outcome: Write generic types and methods whose constraints state exactly the capabilities they need.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Retain the element type) and Example B (Preserve a generic relationship) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The same method returns an int or a string without object casts. Swap preserves the element type, and a tie remains a valid value.

lessons.title: Delegates, closures and events
lessons.outcome: Use delegates, closures and events, including what a closure captures and how to unsubscribe.
lessons.lab: Write a transformation method accepting Func<int,int>.
lessons.verification: Applying value * 10 gives 10, 20 and 30 and leaves the input unchanged.

lessons.title: LINQ, deferred execution and materialization
lessons.outcome: Write LINQ queries and predict when deferred execution observes later source changes.
lessons.lab: Build a deterministic report selecting, transforming and ordering records.
lessons.verification: The report is apple=5 then pear=2; fig with quantity 0 is filtered out.

lessons.title: Grouping, joins and data grain
lessons.outcome: Group and join data at an explicit grain without duplicating or dropping records.
lessons.lab: Build a report joining unique item metadata to item totals.
lessons.verification: Each item appears once with its total: pear=5 and apple=4.

lessons.title: Iterators and lazy sequence contracts
lessons.outcome: Write lazy iterators with yield return and validate their arguments at the call boundary.
lessons.lab: Implement a lazy sequence of cumulative totals.
lessons.verification: 1, 2, 3 produces 1, 3, 6; an empty input produces nothing.

lessons.title: Exceptions and preserving failure meaning
lessons.outcome: Throw and catch exceptions that keep invalid input, environment failures and their causes distinct.
lessons.lab: Define an import API with distinct invalid-input and storage-failure outcomes.
lessons.verification: Valid input returns 3; bad text and unavailable storage end in different exception types.

lessons.title: Disposable resources and deterministic cleanup
lessons.outcome: Release disposable resources deterministically with using, including when an exception occurs.
lessons.lab: Write a helper that reads from a caller-owned stream without closing it.
lessons.verification: The helper returns data and the caller's stream is still readable afterward.

lessons.title: Files, paths and local data ownership
lessons.outcome: Read and write files with explicit encodings inside an owned temporary folder that is always cleaned up.
lessons.lab: Build a temporary-file round trip for a small inventory report.
lessons.verification: The report reads back unchanged and the temporary folder is gone afterward.

lessons.title: JSON contracts and schema evolution
lessons.outcome: Serialize JSON contracts and validate decoded data before trusting it.
lessons.lab: Write a decoder returning explicit validation errors for missing name and negative quantity.
lessons.verification: A valid item gives no errors; a missing name with quantity -1 gives two errors.

lessons.title: Dates, durations and culture-independent data
lessons.outcome: Represent instants and durations with DateTimeOffset and format them independently of culture.
lessons.lab: Build a duration report using fixed UTC timestamps.
lessons.verification: 22:30 to 01:15 UTC is reported as 165 minutes.

lessons.title: Testing contracts with meaningful counterexamples
lessons.outcome: Write table-driven tests with boundary cases that a plausible wrong implementation fails.
lessons.lab: Write table-driven checks for your inventory quantity validator.
lessons.verification: All four rows pass, including both edges of the 0 to 1000 range.

lessons.title: Async, await and task completion
lessons.outcome: Write async methods that await results, propagate failures and keep input order with Task.WhenAll.
lessons.lab: Write an async method returning a validated total.
lessons.verification: Parts 2 and 5 produce the validated total 7.

lessons.title: Cooperative cancellation and bounded waiting
lessons.outcome: Cancel work cooperatively with CancellationToken while keeping already committed results.
lessons.lab: Write an operation that stops cooperatively and preserves already committed work.
lessons.verification: Processing stops before item 3, and items 1 and 2 remain committed.

lessons.title: Bounded channels and producer-consumer ownership
lessons.outcome: Connect producers and consumers through bounded channels with explicit completion.
lessons.lab: Build a bounded producer-consumer pipeline with explicit writer completion.
lessons.verification: The consumer receives five items, 1 to 5, and the sum is 15.

lessons.title: Composition project: a deterministic import service
lessons.outcome: Build a deterministic, cancellable import service that keeps per-item results and rejection counts.
lessons.lab: Build a per-item result while preserving the rejected count.
lessons.verification: pear has 2 accepted units and one rejected record is counted.

lessons.title: Threads, locks and compound invariants
lessons.outcome: Protect compound invariants with a lock so concurrent updates never expose a half-finished change.
lessons.lab: Implement a locked transfer preserving the sum of two balances.
lessons.verification: After ten concurrent transfers of 5 the balances are 50 and 50, still summing to 100.

lessons.title: Atomic operations and concurrent collections
lessons.outcome: Use Interlocked and concurrent collections with pure update functions for correct concurrent counts.
lessons.lab: Build a concurrent frequency counter using pure update functions.
lessons.verification: a is counted 3 times and b once.

lessons.title: Span, slices and memory lifetime
lessons.outcome: Use Span and ReadOnlySpan to slice data without copying while respecting their lifetime rules.
lessons.lab: Write a synchronous span helper counting separators.
lessons.verification: a,b,c has two separators and an empty span has none.

lessons.title: Garbage collection, pooling and retained memory
lessons.outcome: Rent and return pooled buffers with finally and reason about retained memory.
lessons.lab: Write a pooled-buffer helper with finally-based return.
lessons.verification: Summing the first four slots gives 10.

lessons.title: Algorithmic complexity and measured performance
lessons.outcome: Compare an algorithm's work with and without an index while keeping the same equality policy.
lessons.lab: Compare repeated list scans with one built index while preserving equality policy.
lessons.verification: Both approaches find 2 of the 3 queries.

lessons.title: Validation, regular expressions and bounded input
lessons.outcome: Validate bounded input with non-backtracking regular expressions and separate domain rules.
lessons.lab: Validate a structured identifier and then check its domain-specific reserved words.
lessons.verification: report_2 is accepted; admin and 2report are rejected for different reasons.

lessons.title: HTTP clients, status contracts and offline transport tests
lessons.outcome: Call HTTP services through an injected HttpClient and test status and content contracts offline.
lessons.lab: Write a client method accepting a supplied HttpClient and CancellationToken.
lessons.verification: The method returns 4 from the fixture handler without any network access.

lessons.title: Domain architecture and dependency direction
lessons.outcome: Separate a domain core from its adapters so validation and time are testable without infrastructure.
lessons.lab: Extract the inventory aggregation into a transport-independent core.
lessons.verification: Quantities 2, -1 and 3 aggregate to total 5 with one rejection.

lessons.title: API design and the prepared ASP.NET project
lessons.outcome: Design an HTTP API contract and run it in the prepared ASP.NET project with real responses.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Map a valid request) and Example B (Reject before claiming success) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: Valid input maps to the created outcome. Invalid requests produce 400 decisions.

lessons.title: Security boundaries, secrets and untrusted data
lessons.outcome: Apply allowlists and redaction at trust boundaries so errors stay useful without leaking secrets.
lessons.lab: Design an allowlist of fields safe to include in an import error.
lessons.verification: The visible error keeps line, field and reason and drops the token.

lessons.title: Projects, packages and reproducible builds
lessons.outcome: Explain restore, build, run and publish, and check the target framework a build actually produced.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Expose environment facts without overclaiming) and Example B (Read the compiled target framework) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The running framework generation is compatible with the declared classroom target. The compiled program reports .NETCoreApp,Version=v10.0, the framework its project targeted, and runs on a .NET 10 runtime.

lessons.title: Diagnostics, structured events and operational evidence
lessons.outcome: Emit structured events and counts that account for every submitted record.
lessons.lab: Instrument your import project with submitted, accepted and rejected counts.
lessons.verification: 5 submitted records split into 3 accepted and 2 rejected.

lessons.title: Reflection, native boundaries and AOT tradeoffs
lessons.outcome: Weigh reflection against typed access and explain what trimming and AOT require.
lessons.lab: Replace string-based access in a small report with a typed projection.
lessons.verification: The typed projection sums the counts to 7.

lessons.title: Modern C# features and version-aware readability
lessons.outcome: Use C# 12 to 14 features such as collection expressions, primary constructors and null-conditional assignment where they make code clearer.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Use a target-typed collection) and Example B (Keep constructor policy visible) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The target types select array and list representations. The supplied factor is used by the instance operation, nameof(List<>) is List, missing?.Capacity = 32 leaves the null builder alone, and \e is the escape character.

lessons.title: Resilience, idempotency and unknown outcomes
lessons.outcome: Make retried operations idempotent by storing receipts and rejecting conflicting reuse of an identifier.
lessons.lab: Implement a result lookup that does not execute the command again.
lessons.verification: Both calls return receipt 30, and the command ran only once.

lessons.title: Capstone: a reviewable .NET data application
lessons.outcome: Build, test and review a complete .NET data application across a domain library and an API adapter.
lessons.lab: Reproduce Example A (Build a stable valid report) and Example B (Preserve rejected data accounting) and explain each check.
lessons.verification: The sorted report is a=3;b=6. A valid zero remains in the report while two invalid rows are counted.
